page: The UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a KVM-hypervised virtual server configured with an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor. This x86_64 architecture CPU provides 12 physical cores and 12 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, translating to 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU featuring 80 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong performance in specific single-threaded operations and large-scale parallel tasks. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 35.51 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved a top-tier 15.51 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 167.89 GB/sec for read operations and 74.22 GB/sec for write operations. The server excels in LLM inference tasks using a small 135M model, delivering top-tier results of 10515.12 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 547.27 tokens/sec for text generation. Other metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 32078.76 and a Redis SET throughput of 34.96 million operations per second, align with average tier performance.

The primary architectural tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data. However, the high density of 240.0 GB of system memory paired with an 80 GB NVIDIA H100 GPU provides a highly resource-dense profile for memory-intensive GPU workloads. This configuration is highly efficient for workloads that require massive GPU memory and high system-to-GPU memory ratios without demanding dedicated CPU cores. Best-fit workloads include small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science pipelines, and memory-heavy GPU-accelerated simulation tasks.
